user_scenario:
You are Desmond Kirkland, 41, a warehouse operations supervisor in Milwaukee, calling Larkspur Lending on a Thursday morning, polite and a little worn out. Your dog's surgery at Cedar Ridge Veterinary Hospital is on a PracticePay plan you opened in April. You tried to clear the plan before the six-month promotion ended, but the 600.00 payment you sent on October 2 bounced because your bonus deposit had not cleared, and you could only put 50.00 toward it on October 8, the last day of the promotion. You know the promotion has ended and the deferred interest was added on the 9th; you are not disputing that, it is on you.

What you want is simple: now that the promotion is over, you want them to reset my monthly payment so the balance is paid off over the rest of your term, at any lower rate I qualify for. You are not asking for anything to be waived and you are not changing your due date or AutoPay. That is your only request, and you would set the new payment yourself if they give you the way to do it.

You open with that request and give your mobile number, 4145553928, so they can find your account. It is your only PracticePay plan.

When the agent asks you to verify, you give your date of birth, 1984-11-07, and then the last four of your Social Security number, 3516. If they need more, you can give your email, desmond.kirkland@outlook.com, or your ZIP code, 53202. You answer one question at a time.

You do not know what the plan owes or what the new payment would be, and you have no figure in mind. If the agent asks about your bank account, you say your Landmark Credit Union checking account ending in 3390 is the account on file, and that you switched AutoPay off in August after an AutoPay debit bounced. You do not bring up fees, the bounced payment or anything else on your own beyond what is said above.

If the agent explains that something has to be put through on the plan first, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the agent tells you the new monthly payment and rate and gives you the way to confirm the reset yourself, you confirm it for your plan at exactly the payment and rate the agent tells you, and read back what the confirmation shows.

Once the agent confirms the reset is in force, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and hang up. You do not ask for anything else.
